metadata.description: Accepted, independently verified entries — the production lexicon. Includes contested entries (gloss null) that present scholarly uncertainty to the reader.
metadata.score_range: 1-5, all axes now scored (surprise null for contested entries, which carry no gloss)
metadata.forms: Optional per-entry list of derived words sharing the entry's etymon (governor -> govern, government). Each form has word, gloss, part_of_speech, verification_source, and optional plural / surprise_score overrides; everything else is inherited from the parent entry.

entries.note: Juno Moneta's temple on the Capitoline housed the Roman mint.

Theories: 'beech', perhaps beechwood tablets for runes ('generally referred, despite phonetic difficulties' — etymonline; Wiktionary notes beech-bark writing is unknown); PIE *bʰeh₂g- 'to allot', first a letter or ownership mark (Wiktionary).
Theories: Greek kauma 'heat of the sun' — the noontime stillness (etymonline 'probably', Wiktionary 'may'); Latin calere 'be hot'; a Germanic *kalmaz 'cold, frozenness' (Wiktionary).
Theories: 'earthling', from *hūm- 'earth' as in humus (Wiktionary 'perhaps'; etymonline 'partially', with 'no settled explanation of the sound changes'); simply related to homo 'man'.
